subject: When I told Dave that I would, in fact, take it personally if he didn't cover my...
posts:
When professional duty dissolves into personal vibes, public interest is the first casualty.

Journalism Vibe Dispute
Evidence: objective reporting, personal grievance, social gatekeeping
#Media #Democracy

A journalist claims to be defending democracy by demanding coverage of a critical story, expecting professional standards to dictate editorial choices.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The interaction devolves into a personal dispute over social vibes and party invites, reducing a systemic issue to an interpersonal power struggle.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
What is framed as a defense of democratic institutions is actually a localized conflict over personal validation and social access.
An independent writer publicly calls out an editor for refusing to cover an alleged attack on democracy, citing a clash of personal vibes rather than professional disagreement.

The Bright Side:
Calling out gatekeeping in media can sometimes expose how personal networks and subjective biases dictate what news actually reaches the public.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The writer frames this on the plane of WHY (democratic duty). In reality, it operates on WHO (personal ego and social access).

It is a bait-and-switch: public interest is used to force personal validation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the high-minded defense of democracy and the petty interpersonal grievance...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The systemic value of journalism is extracted to fuel a localized social media dispute, shrinking the field of benefit.

The Unavoidable Truth: When news coverage depends on personal vibes, the public loses.

The Unavoidable Lie: That demanding personal attention is the same as defending democracy.

Alethekanon:
This is a structural boundary failure. When professional channels are replaced by social vibes, objective criteria disappear, leaving only raw interpersonal leverage.

Awwthekanon:
It is exhausting to feel unheard when you are trying to share something important. We all want our work to be valued for its substance, not just our social vibe.

Brothekanon:
Bro, if your 'attack on democracy' story gets blocked because you gave off bad party vibes, maybe change your pitch. Demanding a write-up is a bold strategy.
